nodes.description: HER performance in 1 mol L^{-1} PBS (neutral)
nodes.source_text: under neutral conditions, the pristine Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF achieves -10mAcm^{-2} at 89mV without phase reconstruction, which outperforms that of Pt/C at the current densities above -50mA cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-linking nanosheets with smooth surfaces are uniformly grown on nickel foam for Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the scanning electron microscope (SEM) image of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4/NF (Figure 1b), cross-linking nanosheets with smooth surfaces are uniformly grown on the nickel skeleton.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms sheet-like structure of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1d, the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image further confirms the sheet-like structure of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows amorphous-crystalline interfaces in Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF with lattice fringes spacing of 0.486 nm corresponding to (-002) plane of CoC_2O_4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Figure 1e shows the amorphous-crystalline interfaces. In the crystalline phase, lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.486 nm can be observed, corresponding to the (-002) plane of CoC_2O_4, which is slightly larger than the lattice spacing of standard CoC_2O_4.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF shows characteristic diffraction peaks corresponding to monoclinic CoC_2O_4 (JCPDS 25-0251) with peaks slightly shifted toward lower angles indicating lattice expansion due to Ni^{2+} incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1f, the characteristic diffraction peaks of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 correspond to JCPDS 25-0251, which belongs to the monoclinic CoC_2O_4. Interestingly, compared with the standard CoC_2O_4, the characteristic peaks of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 are slightly shifted toward lower angles.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS element mappings show uniform distribution of Co, Ni, C, O, and N elements in Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) element mappings of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI / NF, uniform distribution of Co, Ni, C, O, and N elements can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks corresponding to Ni^{2+} with 0.26 eV shift to higher binding energy and Co 2p peaks with 0.51 eV shift in Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF vs Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4/NF, demonstrating strong electronic coupling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows the signals of Ni 2p in both Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 / NF and Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI / NF, which corresponds to Ni^{2+}. In addition, compared with Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 / NF, the photoelectron peaks of Ni 2p for Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI / NF shift to high binding energy by 0.26 eV. A similar increase of binding energy (0.51 eV) is also observed in the Co 2p region corresponding to Co^{2+}.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES shows Co and Ni K-edges in Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4/NF close to divalent oxides, shifting to higher energies after PANI hybridization indicating delocalized electronic density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) shows similar results to XPS. Both Ni and Co in Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 / NF display an oxidation state which is close to that of divalent oxide. After the formation of the hybrid interface with PANI, the K-edges of both Ni and Co are shifted to higher energies, thus exhibiting a delocalized electronic density.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier transform EXAFS shows PANI layer significantly affects peak positions and amplitudes of first coordination shell Ni-O and Co-O peaks with no significant coordination structure changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier transform of the extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS), it can be observed that the PANI layer has a significant effect on the corresponding peak positions and amplitude peaks of the first coordination shell Ni - O and Co - O. There were no significant changes.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance R_ct of 1.32 ohm for Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS Nyquist curves further manifest the efficient promotion of electron transfer at the organic-inorganic hybrid interface. As displayed in Figure 3d, Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/ NF shows a smaller charge transfer resistance (R_ct,1.32 ohm).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV for electrochemically active surface area estimation gives C_dl = 50.81 mF cm^{-2} for Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF vs 2.78 mF cm^{-2} for Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of pristine Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 / NF is only 2.78 mF cm^{-2} (Figure 3f). With the PANI deposition, the C_dl value is significantly increased to 50.81 mF cm^{-2}, suggesting that the construction of organic-inorganic hybrid interfaces can provide more active site exposure.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES verifies Co:Ni ratio does not change significantly after HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: First, the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) results verify that the ratio of Co to Ni does not change significantly after the reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER XRD shows phase transformation from Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI to Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2@PANI with characteristic diffraction peaks shifted to lower angles compared to standard Co(OH)_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4a shows the phase transformation of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI to Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2@PANI during HER, which is similar to the recent reports. Compared with the standard Co(OH)_2, the characteristic diffraction peaks of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2@PANI are shifted to lower angles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER XPS of Co 2p and Ni 2p shows higher binding energies for Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2@PANI compared to Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2, consistent with pre-HER binding energy differences.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures 4b,c, the photoelectron peaks of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2@ PANI formed by oxalate after phase remodeling are compared with Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2 in the Co 2p and Ni 2p regions. The higher binding energy of Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2@ PANI can be observed, which is consistent with the corresponding binding energy difference between Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4 and Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@ PANI/NF before HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER SEM shows hexagonal sheet structure of hydroxide with rough texture surface similar to PANI layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, in Figure 4d, a hexagonal sheet structure belonging to the hydroxide is shown in the SEM images after HER. The surface of the hexagonal nanosheets displays a rough texture.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER TEM reveals amorphous-crystalline interfaces between Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2 and PANI.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM and HRTEM images reveal the existence of amorphous-crystalline interfaces between Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}(OH)_2 and PANI.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle test shows Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@PANI/NF water drop contact angle decreases from 39.87° to 29.66° in 60 s, indicating superior hydrophilicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4@ PANI/NF, the water drop contact angle quickly decreases from 39.87° to 29.66° at the same time, manifesting the superior hydrophilicity compared with Co_{0.59}Ni_{0.41}C_2O_4/ NF.
